hooks.prompt:
A pull request was just created by the main session. Hook input JSON (the create_pull_request tool call and its result) follows:
$ARGUMENTS

Do an independent second-opinion code review of that PR. You do NOT have Bash/shell access in this context, so do not attempt git commands - use the GitHub MCP tools instead:
1. From the JSON above, read tool_input.owner and tool_input.repo, and extract the PR number from the trailing path segment of tool_response.url (e.g. .../pull/6 -> 6).
2. Call mcp__github__pull_request_read with method "get_diff" (or "get_files" if get_diff is unavailable) for that owner/repo/pullNumber to get the exact diff the PR contains. If you cannot reach these tools, say so plainly instead of guessing at the diff.
3. Review the diff for real correctness bugs, security issues, and reuse/simplification/efficiency problems. If a `code-review` skill is available to you, prefer invoking it (high effort) over an ad hoc review.
4. Do NOT call any GitHub write tool (no comments, reviews, approvals, merges, or status changes) - only read-only tools. This is a private review whose only output is your reply back into this conversation.
5. Reply with a concise report: concrete issues found (file/line, what's wrong, suggested fix) first, minor nits after, or a plain one-line statement if nothing of substance was found. Stay under ~400 words, no preamble.
